key_insight: A CT-informed Gaussian-splat representation captures patient-specific respiratory motion to produce dynamic, view-consistent airway renderings, enabling accurate endoscopic video-to-CT registration without requiring breath-hold protocols.
problem_solved: Respiratory motion deforms the airway by 5–20 mm, causing CT-to-body divergence that limits bronchoscopy localization; current breath-hold protocols are hard to reproduce and disrupt clinical workflow.
method: Initialize a dense Gaussian-splat representation of the airway geometry from the preoperative CT as a prior for appearance and structure.
Fit a low-dimensional, patient-specific respiratory deformation model that animates the CT-informed splats across breathing phases.
Optimize alignment to intraoperative endoscopic video via view-consistent rendering and registration, producing a dynamic CT-to-video correspondence in real time.
impact: Demonstrates how combining medical-image priors with neural/point-based rendering yields clinically usable, patient-specific dynamic models—reducing reliance on protocol constraints and improving registration robustness for image-guided procedures.

paper_title: Stop Holding Your Breath: CT-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Bronchoscopy
paper_authors: Andrea Dunn Beltran, Daniel Rho, Aarav Mehta, Xinqi Xiong, Raúl San José Estépar
